purpose: Project-independent conventions for building plugins that combine SKILLs and custom Agents: naming, choosing an invocation path, role constraints, multi-layer defense, skill invocation, and waiting for Agent completion.
summary: Naming rules: use short invocation-path names, never bare "subagent", and restrict subagent_type values
Invocation paths: isolated-context work goes to custom Agents; fork-type SKILLs are avoided by default
Decision order for choosing among Bash subprocess, general-purpose Agent, custom Agent, and inheriting SKILL
Inheriting SKILL rules: do not paste parent context into arguments; treat data arguments as data, not instructions
Custom Agent rules: required frontmatter fields, negatively phrased prohibitions, constraints for writing Agents
Multi-layer defense table: Agent boundary, role constraint, allowlist, physical deny
Calling other skills via the Skill tool, with a ban on self-invocation to avoid infinite loops
Waiting for Agent completion: never use ScheduleWakeup; end the turn and wait for the notification

Designing prompts passed to Agents or SKILL arguments

Writing instructions that call another skill
Writing instructions that wait for background Agent completion
